sections.html:
Two offices carry most of the work, and they sit in different buildings. The Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bills from Room 103 at 70 North Alexander Street in Toccoa, in the same government building as the county tag office. Weekday hours end at 4:45 in the afternoon. Call (706) 886-4753 or write to PO Box 187, Toccoa, GA 30577. The Tax Commissioner's website is maintained separately from the county's.

For values and homestead forms, call the Tax Assessor at (706) 886-7435. Returns also go there, because the assessors, not the Tax Commissioner, handle that job in Stephens County. Appraisers who visit a parcel carry photo ID and drive a marked county vehicle, usually after an appeal, a return or new construction.

Three rates apply to every parcel: Georgia's, Stephens County's and the Stephens County School System's. A fourth, the Toccoa city rate, is added for homes inside Toccoa city limits, so an in-town house carries one more layer than a rural parcel that only uses a Toccoa mailing address.

Stephens County taxes 40 percent of a property's market value, and each mill of tax equals $1 per $1,000 of that taxed amount. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education pick the rates. If you are unsure whether the address is in the city or the county, ask the Tax Assessor which digest holds the parcel.

sections.h2: Deadlines for returns, homestead and appeals
sections.html:
Stephens County property tax dates and rules
TopicRule
Who is chargedWhoever owns the property on January 1
Return seasonJanuary 1 through April 1, at the Tax Assessor
Same-year homesteadApply by April 1; a later filing waits for the next year
Bills on real estate and business personal propertyGenerally due November 15
Appeal of a noticeMust reach the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date
Skipping a required return10% on the value left off, plus interest
Refund of erroneous taxWritten claim to the commissioners within 3 years

Refunds cover errors of fault, not valuation disputes. Business personal property needs a yearly return by April 1, and real estate owners with no changes can skip one.

Stephens County offers these exemptions:

  • Standard: $2,000 taken from the assessed value of the owner's primary residence, covering state, county and school tax, though municipal school levies are excepted.
  • Seniors 65 and up: an added local exemption, and another one if the owner's and spouse's net income did not top $10,000 the year before.
  • Age 62 school exemption: same $10,000 income ceiling, and it cannot exceed $10,000 of assessed value.
  • Floating inflation-proof exemption: owners 62 and up, with total household income under $30,000.
  • Disabled former service members: $50,000, passing to an unremarried surviving spouse or minor children.

Ownership and residence both have to be in place on January 1. An exemption renews itself unless ownership changes, which means a buyer files fresh. A tax deferral is a further option for owners 62 and older at $15,000 of gross income or below. A state Homeowners Tax Relief Grant that once showed up as a bill credit was withdrawn in 2008.

Stephens County has 27,854 people as of mid-2025, up 4.0% from 26,780 at the 2020 base, spread over 12,461 housing units. Owners live in 73.6% of those units. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $175,300, a typical rent is $820, and median household income is $54,754. Most of the county's 178.86 square miles are outside any compact city grid, so expect rural and in-town parcels to be taxed differently.

Property is taxable in the county where it sits, and the categories go beyond the house itself. Business equipment is assessed at 40 percent. Timber on the lot is treated differently, since it is taxed only when sold or harvested, and then at full market value. If you have timber or business equipment in an outbuilding, ask the Tax Assessor how each is carried on the digest.

Vehicle owners renew their registration and pay ad valorem tax every year in the 30 day period that ends on their birthday, and a newly bought vehicle must be registered within 30 days. The tag office is in the Stephens County Government Building at 70 N. Alexander Street, Room 103, with weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00. This registration is separate from the real estate bill.

Other deed related services include recording a plat, trade name registration and power of attorney filings, which can matter if an heir or an agent signs for the owner.

The county's deed charges are:

  • Transfer tax of $1 per $1,000 of money paid.
  • A $25 filing fee.
  • A $5 blank deed form.
  • 50 cents a page for copies.

Per recorded deed, fifty cents of that tax is kept by the county and the rest goes to the state. The grantor's signature must be witnessed and notarized, and the clerk can help calculate what is due.

Warranty deeds must carry a transfer tax form whether or not money changes hands, and the forms can be completed online at the state clerks' authority site. Filing a deed is not required for it to be legal, but filing protects the owner. A closing attorney usually prepares the deed.

sections.h2: Paying or looking up your bill
sections.html:
Start at the county's Online Payments page, then use the Tax Assessor's online record search or tax estimator to look up a parcel.

A seller closing late in the year should agree with the buyer on who covers a bill charged to the January 1 owner. Call the Tax Commissioner for your parcel's balance ahead of any contract signing, and expect the payoff to come out of your sale proceeds. Unpaid tax can lead to a levy and sale, so clear any balance before you list, or have it paid at closing from your proceeds.

If you are selling an inherited house, the same offices apply. The deed work may involve a power of attorney or other filings at the clerk, so ask the clerk what to bring before you travel to Toccoa, and ask the Tax Assessor whether the late owner's homestead exemption must be refiled by the heir.

Bring the parcel number, your deed and your last bill when you call or visit. If you want to dispute a value, remember that the appeal must reach the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date, and one the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: What is the usual payment date for a Stephens County tax bill?
faqs.a: Real estate and business personal property bills are generally due November 15. Check the date on your own bill, or call (706) 886-4753.

faqs.q: When must a Stephens County homestead application be filed?
faqs.a: April 1. A later filing takes effect the year after. Applications go to the Tax Assessor, and you must have lived in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Stephens County assessment notice?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date, counted by when the appeal is received. An appeal the assessors do not settle moves to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Do Toccoa residents pay extra property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Residents inside Toccoa city limits pay the Toccoa city millage in addition to the Georgia, Stephens County and Stephens County School System millage.

faqs.q: What does the county charge in transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: $1 per $1,000 of money paid, with fifty cents per deed staying in the county. Ask the Clerk of Court to confirm the figure for your sale.
